title: Test design: from manual test cases to automation
summary: Turn test cases into tests: preconditions → fixtures/hooks, steps → actions, expected results → assertions. One behaviour per test, independent, named like the case.
why: Your manual QA experience is the hard part of automation: knowing what to test. This lesson maps that knowledge onto code so your suites stay readable and trustworthy.
body:
Good automated tests are: independent (any order, any worker), deterministic (same input → same result), focused (one behaviour, several assertions about it are fine), readable (Arrange–Act–Assert, case ID in the title), and fast (set up data via API, not the UI).

What to automate first: smoke paths, high-risk regressions, data-heavy checks. Keep exploratory and UX judgement manual.

A useful layering: API tests for rules and contracts, a few UI tests per critical journey, visual tests for layout.
objectives: Map a test case onto Arrange–Act–Assert
pitfalls: One giant end-to-end test covering 10 cases.
Tests that depend on previous tests' data.
